# Synthetic account compatibility corpus

`oracle.json` contains 324 synthetic input cases and the unchanged frozen JavaScript validator's accepted canonical result or rejection. It includes supported input versions 1–11 (minimal and rich-history cases), every supported root entity, historical line prices/names, reversals, partial returns, legacy catalog migration, compatibility-only worker/savings records, preferences and explicit invalid/reference/numeric/date cases. The 180 seeded cases use seed `0x02002610`; these are deterministic generated cases without automatic shrinking.

Source: `electron-reference/app/ui/model.js`, SHA-256 `65a9b33cdca42e328d710f1afaa1b0fb42a7778284bd2f07f7c7e77d3d9f07f4`. Node version and timezone from generation are retained in the manifest. The owner retired the Electron tree and generator on 2026-11-12. The JSON expectations remain frozen; source history and its recorded hash preserve provenance. Tests consume these expected results without executing JavaScript. All data is authored test data; this is not a released-installation migration rehearsal or a production-account snapshot.

`test/accounts/codec_test.dart` compares all accepted fields recursively, checks all rejected inputs, canonical roundtrip and normalization idempotence, independent immutable historical relationships, unsupported/invalid error distinction, UTF8/numeric handling and independent incoming/normalized-output 20 MiB limits. Portable output uses two-space indented JSON, preserving the source save-size acceptance profile. The output-limit regression builds 200,000 unique valid expenses whose compact input fits 20 MiB but normalized output exceeds it.

Timestamp compatibility retains original text and tests source ISO, date-only/year-only, US and RFC forms, invalid hour/month/minute, overflow calendar day, hour24 and zero-year behavior. Independent-review regressions additionally cover legacy numeric/English TimeClip limits, source EST/date-only-Z spellings and MAXSAFE remainder neighbors whose temporary prefix exceeds the final-value bound. The remainder compatibility profile preserves the frozen operator grouping and binary64 integer-rounding acceptance through an explicit BigInt-only engine helper; exact and strict-prefix policies remain separate. The finite oracle corpus is evidence for the listed cases, not a proof over every implementation-dependent JavaScript `Date.parse` spelling. The consumer's parser remains subject to independent compatibility review before release. Generic arithmetic/date/identifier rules are consumed from `madar_domain`; restaurant field names, references, migration meanings and source-specific string/timestamp compatibility remain here.

Do not regenerate these expectations from the current Dart implementation. An intentional compatibility change needs independent expected values and review. Tests use synthetic fixtures and never open installed restaurant files.


## Step4 pinned V8 timestamp composers — APP-P2-01

In addition to 324 normal cases, compact 4,127 timestamp cases exercise the independent 4,036-case matrix, 55 primary-source grammar probes, 22 scanner/Unicode/numeral/40-unit/TimeClip boundaries, and 14 expanded-year/offset cases. Expected outcomes are generated by the unchanged frozen full validator, changing only `sales[0].createdAt` in the existing synthetic fixture. Tests inject each timestamp into that fixture and retain the original exact string. No repeated full document is stored per matrix case.

The previous shared numeric/English timezone range assumption was incorrect: V8's legacy composers can consume out-of-range English seconds/colon-offset minutes as an extra date component, while a complete numeric date rejects them. The private parser now adapts the pinned primary tokenizer/ES5/legacy composers. See [primary source, hashes, BSD notice and bounds](../../../docs/reference/legacy-v8-timestamp-compatibility.md). No tested mismatch is waived; independent review still applies.
